analysis: Integration review of the PR: it pins the qualify-sdk CI job to DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT: prod (.github/workflows/release-provider.yml, job env block near head lines 239-242, comment at 181-182). Supporting changes are a changelog entry, a docs update (docs/operations/provider-release.md ~311-320) and a tightened guard test (scripts/test-provider-release-pipeline.py 180-182). The test forbids the resolve-env selector in qualify-sdk and requires exactly one literal 'prod' assignment there. I found no new secrets, permissions, triggers or expression interpolation. qualify-sdk keeps contents: read. The build-provider job still compiles with the resolved environment (head line ~183). The signing job's build-environment smoke checks against ENV_PREFIX and its designated-requirement checks are unchanged, so a dev or staging artifact cannot pass as prod. The change affects only test-time identity defaults. Relevant threats T-034, T-054, T-061 and assets A-011 and A-017 are not weakened, since official-build identity is enforced at signing and registration, which this PR does not touch. I reviewed all prior unit analyses and found no contradictions among them. Unverified items outside the supplied evidence: (1) the qualification composite action's handling of its environment input versus the job-level env var; (2) Package.swift env selection; (3) that the test's regex matches the actual workflow. These are correctness or test-fidelity questions and not demonstrated security regressions. No threat-model update is needed.
